name: Dusky Slate-Blue
lede: Dusky Slate-Blue is a dark, muted blue-grey that our library finds almost identical to plain Charcoal.

sections.title: A slate word, close to charcoal
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature gives the swatch as plate XLIII, hue 49′′′, tone m, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 reads it as a dark grayish blue, about 4 units from the block center [1]. Our library names [[charcoal]] as this color's nearest match, under 3 units away, which is closer than it is to most blues [1][2].

Further out are [[dark-payne-s-grey]] and [[dark-delft-blue]], both under 5 units away, placing this swatch in a tight cluster of near-black blue-greys [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color, as photographed, appears in 425 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.79 percent, more common than 69 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 34 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.0 percent of that period's paintings, 2.4 times the overall rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color [3]. Its most devoted painter is Gustav Klimt, carrying it in 4 of 50 works here, 4.7 times the baseline for his museums [3]. The earliest match in the archive is a 1260 painting, 652 years before the name's 1912 record, so this is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a pigment identification, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

issues: Fixed: the field-notes paragraph (and the matching "field" object) invented painter names ("Guercino and George Bellows") that do not appear anywhere in this slug's painter data (the real most-devoted painter is Gustav Klimt, 4 of 50 works, 4.7x) and an earliest-match painter ("Master of the Franciscan Crucifixes") not supported by the data (fs.fa is null). The presence count (318) and peak-decade stat (1470s/5.8%/4.3x, also baked into the "field" object) didn't match any real field either (real: 425 as-photographed; peak is the 1900s century fact, 2.0%/2.4x). Rewrote the paragraph directly from data/graph/fieldnotes for this slug; removed every unsupported claim rather than inventing a replacement for it.
